Ian — thanks, we can do that. Attaching an initial packet with high-level answers and an annotated network sketch. Ben will follow with the deeper threat annotations and kernel/SBOM notes; Karthik will attach a diagram that separates control plane telemetry from the inference datapath and shows enforcement points.

Quick summary so your risk committee has context before they open the packet:

- Control plane (model management, rollout, and telemetry) is separated from the inference data plane. Control plane traffic is carried over a dedicated management VPC with mutual TLS and mTLS-authenticated agents; customer secrets for model signing/keys are stored in customer-managed KMS/HSM when running Private.
- Data plane (request ingress, KV cache, tokenized sequences, and model runtime) runs on segregated worker pools; runtime only loads model artifacts that have been validated and optionally verified via a model signature check during the model install stage.
- Third-party dependencies: we use OS packages and GPU kernels from validated sources; we provide SBOMs for container images and can provide kernel-version attestations and signatures on request.
- Defenses: allowlist egress policies, sidecar-level egress filtering, prefix/KV caching controls, automated rollback on model behavioral regressions, and audit trails tied to model artifact metadata.

I'll leave detailed annotations to Ben + Karthik. If your committee prefers a single redacted packet (no internal drive links) we can send a PDF export.

Best,
Aisha Rahman
Enterprise Solutions
Redwood Inference

Ian, Priya — adding the threat annotations and concrete operator controls below. Inline notes follow the packet pages (see attached threat_model_annotations_2028-07-10.txt and SBOM csv).

1) Supply chain insertion points (ranked):
   - Model artifact ingestion: unverified model bundles pushed to artifact storage (mitigation: require signed model manifests; enforce signature verification during model install).
   - Build pipelines for container images/kernels: malicious binaries embedded in vendor builds (mitigation: vendor CI attestation, SBOM, signed containers, and reproducible builds).
   - External library/native kernels loaded at runtime: compromised kernel module could subvert runtime memory (mitigation: kernel version allowlist, container sandboxing, and runtime integrity checks).

2) Data-path exfil vectors to watch for:
   - Sidecar egress channels (misconfigured filters allowing arbitrary outbound connections).
   - Prefetch/cache poisoning where adversarial input causes cached outputs to leak across tenants.
   - Telemetry back-channels if control plane agents are not properly isolated.

3) Operator controls we can contractually offer (language suggestions):
   - "Model artifacts deployed to customer workloads MUST be accompanied by signed manifests; Redwood will supply signing keys or support customer-managed keys via KMS/HSM"
   - "SBOM and container image digests for runtime images will be delivered quarterly or on demand for audit"
   - "Egress allowlist enforcement and sidecar-level outbound filtering will be enabled by default for Dedicated and Private deployments"
   - "Audit logs for model installs, signature verification results, and operator rollbacks will be retained for X days (negotiable per contract) and delivered to customer S3 or fed to customer's SIEM via TLS-forwarding"

4) Evidence/Artifacts we can produce quickly:
   - SBOM CSV for runtime images (attached).
   - Kernel and container image digest + signature provenance (attached summary).
   - Behavioral regression testsets used by Redwood Optimize for model rollouts (we can provide sanitized examples).

Notes on severity: supply chain insertions are high-impact but low-probability if signing + SBOM + allowlist are enforced. The biggest practical risk often comes from misconfiguration of outbound filters. We recommend requiring sidecar-level egress deny-by-default + operator attestation.

Ben Carter
Staff Security Engineer, Redwood Inference

--
Attachments: threat_model_annotations_2028-07-10.txt (text), SBOM_and_kernel_signing_summary.csv (csv)

Ian — attaching the updated diagram that explicitly separates the control plane MGT-VPC from customer inference clusters and shows enforcement points we recommend Hightower require. Summary highlights (also included as callouts in the diagram):

- Control plane (management) — mTLS-only control channel; personnel access via bastion + MFA; customer-specific control plane tenancy for Private deployments.
- Inference dataplane — per-tenant worker pools, network namespaces per tenant for Dedicated/Private; sidecar proxies enforce egress allowlist and do per-connection ACLs.
- Artifact verification point — model install stage checks manifest signatures and verifies SBOM/digest before unpacking into runtime. Attestation recorded in audit log item with hash+signer.
- Runtime hardening — seccomp, CPU pinning options for noisy neighbor isolation, GPU driver version pinning.
- Fallbacks — automatic canary rollback if per-step QA fails; automatic routing to a verified model replica in another region if artifact verification fails in a zone.

Drive link: https://drive.redwood.com/shared/HTW/packet-5401 (diagram: network_diagram_controlplane_vs_dataplane_v2.png)

Let me know if you want a single-slide summary suitable for your executive packet.

Karthik Iyer
